claims.claim: Stop-and-restart benching, priced in policies/projects-in-distress.md at roughly $10,000/week of opportunity cost per team member awaiting reassignment, directly erodes the utilization rate that policies/finance-and-billing.md names as 'the primary indicator of financial stability for TTS' — so the displaced work paid for by every project stop/restart decision is measurable utilization-rate degradation across whichever chapter absorbs the benched staff, not just the individual engagement.

RFC 004 (approved 2021-08-03) states cross-TTS hiring is bottlenecked by 'limited TTS Talent, OHRM, and hiring manager / interviewer capacity' and designs the entire bucket-hiring pilot around rationing that scarce capacity. RFC 003 (approved two days later, 2021-08-05) commits the new Senior Cybersecurity Advisor to 'collaborate and advise on cybersecurity hiring needs at TTS' in partnership with Talent, adding coordination demand onto the same Talent/OHRM capacity RFC 004 just declared saturated — with neither RFC referencing the other's claim on that resource.

org/solutions-portfolio.md states every standing TTS initiative is 'funded the same way engagement work is: out of reimbursements recovered against agreements that each name a period of performance' — TTS's only described revenue mechanism runs through a client agreement with a bounded period of performance. RFC 003 explicitly places the Senior Cybersecurity Advisor's work (coordination, advice, hiring support, training) outside any single engagement and defers identifying 'a funding source for this role' until after the position is approved and staffed, meaning the bet to add this headcount is made before anyone has confirmed it fits the org's only documented way of paying for standing work.

policies/finance-and-billing.md assigns TTS leadership the explicit governance role of 'weighing capacity projections in pipeline and hiring decisions' before commitments are made. RFC 003 inverts that sequence for its own recommendation: it approves adding the Senior Cybersecurity Advisor first and states 'the initial part of this role will be to determine a budget, staff and hiring' — pushing the capacity/funding weighing the finance policy calls a leadership function onto the person hired into the role, after the hiring decision is already made rather than before.
